spec.description: How far each Chilean GNSS station moved in a window you pick from the earthquakes since 2013: arrows for the horizontal shift, colour for the vertical, plate boundaries and the M6+ events on the map, and the east, north and up series of any station with its trend. Open data from Data Observatory (Geo-Sismos) and USGS. The Plus map adds a card per station with its path through the window, in the component the latitude-time map shows.
Where the positions come from, how fresh they are, and why an arrow is not the ground distance.
spec.title: About the data

options.content:
### Where the data comes from

- **Stations and series**: [Geo-Sismos](https://geosismos.cl/explorador), published by the [Data Observatory](https://www.dataobservatory.net/). The raw RINEX comes from the National Seismological Center of the University of Chile; Data Observatory processes it with GFZRNX and PRIDE PPP-AR and publishes each station's daily position. Open data. Cite it as Data Observatory Foundation (2026), [DOI 10.57716/5j4w-3b13](https://doi.org/10.57716/5j4w-3b13).
- **Coverage**: 158 stations, from 1 January 2013 to the day in *Latest data*, which is the newest day in the station catalog. This is not a live feed: the catalog is rewritten every few weeks.
- **Earthquakes**: the [USGS ComCat](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/) catalogue, every M6+ event between 15°S and 60°S, east of 115°W. Public domain.
- **Plate boundaries**: PB2002 by Bird (2003), *An updated digital model of plate boundaries*, G³ 4(3), 1027, in the [GeoJSON copy by Hugo Ahlenius](https://github.com/fraxen/tectonicplates) (ODC-By). It is the same model the Geo-Sismos explorer draws.

### How the shift is measured

The window is the time picker, or a click on the earthquake timeline. A station's shift is its position on the last day of the window minus its position on the first, in east, north and up. The Geo-Sismos network service answers only for those two exact days, and many stations have a gap on one of them, so the dashboard also asks a few days inward from each end (up to an eighth of the window, at most ten days, so a window around an earthquake never crosses it) and keeps the outermost day each station has. A station's tooltip on the map gives the two days used. A window that ends after the newest published day is cut at that day.

The map measures the **time brush**, not the whole window: each station's shift from its first step inside the brush to its last, as one arrow lying on the ground (the horizontal shift, pointing the way it went, coloured by centimetres) and one standing on it (up and blue where it rose, down and red where it sank). That is the quantity a geodesist reads off two epochs, and it is what the table gives for the whole window; drag the brush to a narrower span, or play it, to watch the network move through the window. Sizes are relative to the largest shift of the brush, *Arrow size* pixels; *Arrow growth* is logarithmic by default, because shifts in Chile run from millimetres of loading to metres at a great earthquake, and on a linear scale everything but the largest becomes a dot. Easter Island (RAPA) sits on the Nazca plate and moves about 7 cm a year to the east; in long windows it sets the size of the mainland arrows, which is what the logarithmic growth is for.

### The paths and the whole network

The *Path* sparklines in the table and the latitude-time map read a file built once on each instance by `datasets/geosismos/build.sh` (every station's daily position, from the same Geo-Sismos API; run it again when the catalog is rewritten). The build drops the days the source flags as outliers and any day more than 10 cm off the median of the two months around it, which removes a few unflagged runs of metres-off days while keeping real jumps. The window is cut into at most about 120 buckets (a day for windows up to four months, a week for about two years, longer beyond) and each bucket is the median of its days, measured from the station's first bucket in the window. Without the file both panels are empty; everything else works.

### How to read the series

The daily positions are drawn in millimetres from the station's first good day in the window, so the last point of the east and north lines is the arrow on the map. The trend is an ordinary least-squares line over the good days. When an M7+ earthquake within 500 km of the station falls inside the window, a trend would average over the jump, so the chart gives the jump instead: the mean of the three good days after the event minus the mean of the three before. Days the source flags as outliers are grey dots, left out of the line and the trend.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT id, latitude, epoch_ms(span_from)::DOUBLE AS a, epoch_ms(span_to)::DOUBLE + 86400000 AS b, days
FROM $avail
ORDER BY latitude DESC, a

spec.description: Every unbroken run of daily positions in the Geo-Sismos catalog, one row per station, ordered from north to south. The shaded band is the window: a station needs data near both of its edges to get an arrow. The chosen station is orange. Click a row to choose that station.

spec.description: The span the map measures: each arrow is a station's shift from the first step inside the brush to the last. Drag its edges or the window, step it, or press play. The bars are the stations with a position at each step. Scrolled past, it pins to the top of the page.
spec.title: Time brush · the span the arrows measure

spec.rawSql:
WITH b AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t0 AS TIMESTAMP), min(time)) AS t0,
         coalesce(try_cast($t1 AS TIMESTAMP), max(time)) AS t1
  FROM $spark
),
ends AS (
  SELECT s.id, any_value(s.latitude) AS latitude, any_value(s.longitude) AS longitude,
         arg_min(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
         arg_max(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e1,
         arg_min(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
         arg_max(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n1,
         arg_min(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u0,
         arg_max(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u1,
         count(s.east_mm) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1) AS steps
  FROM $spark s, b
  GROUP BY s.id
),
d AS (
  SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
         e1 - e0 AS east_mm, n1 - n0 AS north_mm, u1 - u0 AS up_mm,
         sqrt((e1 - e0) ^ 2 + (n1 - n0) ^ 2) AS horizontal_mm,
         (degrees(atan2(e1 - e0, n1 - n0)) + 360) % 360 AS azimuth_deg,
         steps
  FROM ends
  -- a shift needs two steps: with one, start and end are the same day
  WHERE steps >= 2
)
SELECT id || ' · ' || ['N', 'NE', 'E', 'SE', 'S', 'SW', 'W', 'NW'][(round(azimuth_deg / 45)::BIGINT % 8 + 1)::BIGINT]
         || ' · up ' || CASE WHEN up_mm >= 0 THEN '+' ELSE '' END || round(up_mm / 10, 1) || ' cm' AS label,
       round(horizontal_mm / 10, 2) AS cm
FROM d
WHERE id = $station

spec.description: The station picked on the map, in the table, on the availability chart or in the dropdown: its horizontal shift over the time brush, the compass direction, and the vertical shift. Empty when it has fewer than two steps inside the brush.

spec.rawSql:
-- Stations with a shift over the brush, inside the drawn shape when there is one.
WITH area AS (
  SELECT list_transform(xs, lambda x: x - 360 * round(coalesce(list_avg(xs), 0) / 360)) AS xs, ys
  FROM (
    SELECT
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
    FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($area, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
  )
),
b AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t0 AS TIMESTAMP), min(time)) AS t0,
         coalesce(try_cast($t1 AS TIMESTAMP), max(time)) AS t1
  FROM $spark
),
ends AS (
  SELECT s.id, any_value(s.latitude) AS latitude, any_value(s.longitude) AS longitude,
         arg_min(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
         arg_max(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e1,
         arg_min(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
         arg_max(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n1,
         arg_min(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u0,
         arg_max(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u1,
         count(s.east_mm) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1) AS steps
  FROM $spark s, b
  GROUP BY s.id
),
d AS (
  SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
         e1 - e0 AS east_mm, n1 - n0 AS north_mm, u1 - u0 AS up_mm,
         sqrt((e1 - e0) ^ 2 + (n1 - n0) ^ 2) AS horizontal_mm,
         (degrees(atan2(e1 - e0, n1 - n0)) + 360) % 360 AS azimuth_deg,
         steps
  FROM ends
  -- a shift needs two steps: with one, start and end are the same day
  WHERE steps >= 2
)
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE horizontal_mm IS NOT NULL)::DOUBLE AS n
FROM d, area
WHERE (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)

spec.description: Stations with a position at two or more steps inside the time brush (inside the drawn shape, when there is one), out of the 158 in the catalog. The others are the small grey dots.
spec.title: Stations with a shift

spec.rawSql:
-- Inside the drawn shape, when there is one.
WITH area AS (
  SELECT list_transform(xs, lambda x: x - 360 * round(coalesce(list_avg(xs), 0) / 360)) AS xs, ys
  FROM (
    SELECT
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
    FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($area, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
  )
)
SELECT id, latitude, epoch_ms(time)::DOUBLE AS time, east_mm, north_mm, up_mm, horizontal_mm
FROM $spark, area
WHERE (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
ORDER BY latitude DESC, time
SELECT epoch_ms(time)::DOUBLE AS t, mag FROM $quakes WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND mag >= 7 ORDER BY t

spec.rawSql:
-- Stations with a shift over the time brush: the dots the arrows stand on,
-- and what a click picks.
WITH b AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t0 AS TIMESTAMP), min(time)) AS t0,
         coalesce(try_cast($t1 AS TIMESTAMP), max(time)) AS t1
  FROM $spark
),
ends AS (
  SELECT s.id, any_value(s.latitude) AS latitude, any_value(s.longitude) AS longitude,
         arg_min(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
         arg_max(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e1,
         arg_min(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
         arg_max(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n1,
         arg_min(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u0,
         arg_max(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u1,
         count(s.east_mm) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1) AS steps
  FROM $spark s, b
  GROUP BY s.id
),
d AS (
  SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
         e1 - e0 AS east_mm, n1 - n0 AS north_mm, u1 - u0 AS up_mm,
         sqrt((e1 - e0) ^ 2 + (n1 - n0) ^ 2) AS horizontal_mm,
         (degrees(atan2(e1 - e0, n1 - n0)) + 360) % 360 AS azimuth_deg,
         steps
  FROM ends
  -- a shift needs two steps: with one, start and end are the same day
  WHERE steps >= 2
)
SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
       round(horizontal_mm / 10, 2) AS horizontal_cm,
       round(up_mm / 10, 2) AS up_cm
FROM d
WHERE horizontal_mm IS NOT NULL

-- Stations with no position inside the time brush, or only one: no arrow.
WITH b AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t0 AS TIMESTAMP), min(time)) AS t0,
         coalesce(try_cast($t1 AS TIMESTAMP), max(time)) AS t1
  FROM $spark
),
ends AS (
  SELECT s.id, any_value(s.latitude) AS latitude, any_value(s.longitude) AS longitude,
         arg_min(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
         arg_max(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e1,
         arg_min(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
         arg_max(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n1,
         arg_min(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u0,
         arg_max(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u1,
         count(s.east_mm) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1) AS steps
  FROM $spark s, b
  GROUP BY s.id
),
d AS (
  SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
         e1 - e0 AS east_mm, n1 - n0 AS north_mm, u1 - u0 AS up_mm,
         sqrt((e1 - e0) ^ 2 + (n1 - n0) ^ 2) AS horizontal_mm,
         (degrees(atan2(e1 - e0, n1 - n0)) + 360) % 360 AS azimuth_deg,
         steps
  FROM ends
  -- a shift needs two steps: with one, start and end are the same day
  WHERE steps >= 2
)
SELECT s.id, s.latitude, s.longitude, 'no data in the brush' AS why
FROM $shifts s
LEFT JOIN d ON d.id = s.id
WHERE d.horizontal_mm IS NULL

-- M6+ earthquakes inside the window. The date is text on purpose: a time
-- column would give the map a time filter of its own.
SELECT latitude, longitude, mag, depth_km, place, strftime(time, '%d %b %Y') AS day
FROM $quakes
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
SELECT name, kind, geometry FROM $plates

-- One arrow per station: how it moved horizontally between the two edges of
-- the time brush (its first step inside the brush to its last), lying on the
-- ground, pointing the way it went. The largest of the brush is $arrow pixels;
-- the rest scale against it, linearly or logarithmically ($growth), down to a
-- smallest arrow that stays visible. The colour gives the centimetres.
WITH b AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t0 AS TIMESTAMP), min(time)) AS t0,
         coalesce(try_cast($t1 AS TIMESTAMP), max(time)) AS t1
  FROM $spark
),
ends AS (
  SELECT s.id, any_value(s.latitude) AS latitude, any_value(s.longitude) AS longitude,
         arg_min(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
         arg_max(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e1,
         arg_min(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
         arg_max(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n1,
         arg_min(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u0,
         arg_max(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u1,
         count(s.east_mm) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1) AS steps
  FROM $spark s, b
  GROUP BY s.id
),
d AS (
  SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
         e1 - e0 AS east_mm, n1 - n0 AS north_mm, u1 - u0 AS up_mm,
         sqrt((e1 - e0) ^ 2 + (n1 - n0) ^ 2) AS horizontal_mm,
         (degrees(atan2(e1 - e0, n1 - n0)) + 360) % 360 AS azimuth_deg,
         steps
  FROM ends
  -- a shift needs two steps: with one, start and end are the same day
  WHERE steps >= 2
),
k AS (SELECT max(horizontal_mm) AS hmax, CAST($arrow AS DOUBLE) AS px, try_cast($growth AS DOUBLE) * 1000 AS ref
      FROM d WHERE horizontal_mm > 0)
SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
       round(horizontal_mm / 10, 2) AS horizontal_cm,
       round((degrees(atan2(east_mm, north_mm)) + 360) % 360) AS toward_deg,
       round(greatest(10, k.px * CASE WHEN k.ref IS NULL THEN horizontal_mm / k.hmax
                                      ELSE ln(1 + horizontal_mm / k.ref) / ln(1 + k.hmax / k.ref) END)) AS size_px
FROM d, k
WHERE horizontal_mm > 0

-- One arrow per station that rose (or, in the twin query, sank) between the two
-- edges of the time brush, standing on the ground at the station: blue and
-- pointing up for uplift, red and pointing down for subsidence. Sized like the
-- horizontal arrows, against the largest vertical shift of the brush.
WITH b AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t0 AS TIMESTAMP), min(time)) AS t0,
         coalesce(try_cast($t1 AS TIMESTAMP), max(time)) AS t1
  FROM $spark
),
ends AS (
  SELECT s.id, any_value(s.latitude) AS latitude, any_value(s.longitude) AS longitude,
         arg_min(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
         arg_max(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e1,
         arg_min(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
         arg_max(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n1,
         arg_min(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u0,
         arg_max(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u1,
         count(s.east_mm) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1) AS steps
  FROM $spark s, b
  GROUP BY s.id
),
d AS (
  SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
         e1 - e0 AS east_mm, n1 - n0 AS north_mm, u1 - u0 AS up_mm,
         sqrt((e1 - e0) ^ 2 + (n1 - n0) ^ 2) AS horizontal_mm,
         (degrees(atan2(e1 - e0, n1 - n0)) + 360) % 360 AS azimuth_deg,
         steps
  FROM ends
  -- a shift needs two steps: with one, start and end are the same day
  WHERE steps >= 2
),
k AS (SELECT max(abs(up_mm)) AS umax, CAST($arrow AS DOUBLE) AS px, try_cast($growth AS DOUBLE) * 1000 AS ref
      FROM d WHERE up_mm <> 0)
SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
       round(up_mm / 10, 2) AS up_cm,
       round(greatest(10, k.px * CASE WHEN k.ref IS NULL THEN abs(up_mm) / k.umax
                                      ELSE ln(1 + abs(up_mm) / k.ref) / ln(1 + k.umax / k.ref) END)) AS size_px
FROM d, k
WHERE up_mm > 0

-- One arrow per station that sank (or, in the twin query, rose) between the two
-- edges of the time brush, standing on the ground at the station: blue and
-- pointing up for uplift, red and pointing down for subsidence. Sized like the
-- horizontal arrows, against the largest vertical shift of the brush.
WITH b AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t0 AS TIMESTAMP), min(time)) AS t0,
         coalesce(try_cast($t1 AS TIMESTAMP), max(time)) AS t1
  FROM $spark
),
ends AS (
  SELECT s.id, any_value(s.latitude) AS latitude, any_value(s.longitude) AS longitude,
         arg_min(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
         arg_max(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e1,
         arg_min(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
         arg_max(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n1,
         arg_min(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u0,
         arg_max(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u1,
         count(s.east_mm) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1) AS steps
  FROM $spark s, b
  GROUP BY s.id
),
d AS (
  SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
         e1 - e0 AS east_mm, n1 - n0 AS north_mm, u1 - u0 AS up_mm,
         sqrt((e1 - e0) ^ 2 + (n1 - n0) ^ 2) AS horizontal_mm,
         (degrees(atan2(e1 - e0, n1 - n0)) + 360) % 360 AS azimuth_deg,
         steps
  FROM ends
  -- a shift needs two steps: with one, start and end are the same day
  WHERE steps >= 2
),
k AS (SELECT max(abs(up_mm)) AS umax, CAST($arrow AS DOUBLE) AS px, try_cast($growth AS DOUBLE) * 1000 AS ref
      FROM d WHERE up_mm <> 0)
SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
       round(up_mm / 10, 2) AS up_cm,
       round(greatest(10, k.px * CASE WHEN k.ref IS NULL THEN abs(up_mm) / k.umax
                                      ELSE ln(1 + abs(up_mm) / k.ref) / ln(1 + k.umax / k.ref) END)) AS size_px
FROM d, k
WHERE up_mm < 0

-- One row per station and step for the cards: the component the latitude-time
-- map shows, in mm from the station's first step, through the whole window
-- (the brush does not cut it).
SELECT id, latitude, longitude, time, ${comp:raw} AS value
FROM $spark
WHERE ${comp:raw} IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY id, time

spec.description: Each station's shift between the two edges of the time brush (its first step inside the brush to its last): the arrow lying on the ground points the way it moved horizontally, coloured by centimetres, and the arrow standing on it points up where it rose (blue) or down where it sank (red). Drag, step or play the brush and the arrows follow. Sizes are relative to the largest shift of the brush (Arrow size, Arrow growth). The steps come from datasets/geosismos/build.sh; without it there are no arrows. Small grey dots are stations with no data near one of the ends. Purple rings are the M6+ earthquakes inside the window, sized by magnitude, and the orange lines are the subduction zones of Bird (2003). Click a station to load its series; draw a shape (the polygon or rectangle tool) to keep the counts and the table to the stations inside it. Hover a station for its card: its path through the whole window in the component picked on the latitude-time map (east by default), in millimetres from its first step.
spec.title: GNSS stations · the shift over the time brush · hover a station for its card

spec.rawSql:
-- The station that moved the most over the brush, inside the drawn shape when there is one.
WITH area AS (
  SELECT list_transform(xs, lambda x: x - 360 * round(coalesce(list_avg(xs), 0) / 360)) AS xs, ys
  FROM (
    SELECT
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
    FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($area, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
  )
),
b AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t0 AS TIMESTAMP), min(time)) AS t0,
         coalesce(try_cast($t1 AS TIMESTAMP), max(time)) AS t1
  FROM $spark
),
ends AS (
  SELECT s.id, any_value(s.latitude) AS latitude, any_value(s.longitude) AS longitude,
         arg_min(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
         arg_max(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e1,
         arg_min(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
         arg_max(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n1,
         arg_min(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u0,
         arg_max(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u1,
         count(s.east_mm) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1) AS steps
  FROM $spark s, b
  GROUP BY s.id
),
d AS (
  SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
         e1 - e0 AS east_mm, n1 - n0 AS north_mm, u1 - u0 AS up_mm,
         sqrt((e1 - e0) ^ 2 + (n1 - n0) ^ 2) AS horizontal_mm,
         (degrees(atan2(e1 - e0, n1 - n0)) + 360) % 360 AS azimuth_deg,
         steps
  FROM ends
  -- a shift needs two steps: with one, start and end are the same day
  WHERE steps >= 2
)
SELECT id, round(horizontal_mm / 10, 1) AS cm
FROM d, area
WHERE horizontal_mm IS NOT NULL AND (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
ORDER BY horizontal_mm DESC
LIMIT 1

spec.description: The largest horizontal shift over the time brush, in centimetres, and the station: the largest arrow on the map.
spec.title: Largest shift

spec.rawSql:
-- Server side: the daily east, north and up position of the station picked on
-- the map, in the table, on the availability chart or in the dropdown, in
-- millimetres from its first good day in the window, so the line reads as the
-- same displacement the arrow draws. Days the source flags as outliers are
-- kept, marked, and left out of the line and of the trend.
WITH req AS (
  SELECT http_get(
    'https://d3l3n3l7bvxxh8.cloudfront.net/graphs?id_station='
    || '${station:raw}'
    || '&min_date=' || strftime(CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMP), '%Y-%m-%d')
    || '&max_date=' || strftime(CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMP), '%Y-%m-%d')
  ) AS r
  WHERE regexp_full_match('${station:raw}', '^[A-Z0-9]{4}$')
),
body AS (
  SELECT regexp_replace(r->>'body', '\bNaN\b', 'null')::JSON -> 'data' -> 'graphs' AS g
  FROM req
  WHERE r->>'status' = '200'
),
-- Each component cast to a map from day to {value, outlier} in one pass:
-- looking each day up by key is quadratic, and over the whole record it
-- outlasts the query deadline.
comp AS (
  SELECT 'e' AS k, unnest(map_entries(CAST(g -> 'east' AS MAP(VARCHAR, STRUCT(value DOUBLE, outlier INTEGER))))) AS m FROM body
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'n', unnest(map_entries(CAST(g -> 'north' AS MAP(VARCHAR, STRUCT(value DOUBLE, outlier INTEGER))))) FROM body
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'u', unnest(map_entries(CAST(g -> 'up' AS MAP(VARCHAR, STRUCT(value DOUBLE, outlier INTEGER))))) FROM body
),
days AS (
  SELECT
    m.key::TIMESTAMP AS time,
    max(m.value.value * 1000) FILTER (WHERE k = 'e') AS e,
    max(m.value.value * 1000) FILTER (WHERE k = 'n') AS n,
    max(m.value.value * 1000) FILTER (WHERE k = 'u') AS u,
    coalesce(max(m.value.outlier) FILTER (WHERE k = 'e'), 0) AS out_e,
    coalesce(max(m.value.outlier) FILTER (WHERE k = 'n'), 0) AS out_n,
    coalesce(max(m.value.outlier) FILTER (WHERE k = 'u'), 0) AS out_u
  FROM comp
  GROUP BY time
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    arg_min(e, time) FILTER (WHERE out_e = 0 AND e IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
    arg_min(n, time) FILTER (WHERE out_n = 0 AND n IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
    arg_min(u, time) FILTER (WHERE out_u = 0 AND u IS NOT NULL) AS u0
  FROM days
)
SELECT
  time,
  round(e - e0, 1) AS east_mm,
  round(n - n0, 1) AS north_mm,
  round(u - u0, 1) AS up_mm,
  out_e, out_n, out_u
FROM days, base
ORDER BY time

-- M6+ earthquakes within 500 km of the chosen station, inside the window:
-- the vertical lines on the chart.
SELECT epoch_ms(q.time)::DOUBLE AS t, q.mag, q.place, km
FROM (
  SELECT q.*, round(2 * 6371 * asin(sqrt(
           pow(sin(radians(q.latitude - s.latitude) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(s.latitude)) * cos(radians(q.latitude))
             * pow(sin(radians(q.longitude - s.longitude) / 2), 2)))) AS km
  FROM $quakes q, (SELECT latitude, longitude FROM $shifts WHERE id = $station) s
  WHERE $__timeFilter(q.time)
) q
WHERE km <= 500
ORDER BY t

spec.description: East, north and up position of the chosen station, one sample a day, in millimetres from its first good day in the window, so the end of the east and north lines is the arrow on the map. The dashed line is the trend over the window, with its slope in mm per year; when an M7+ event within 500 km falls inside the window, the title gives its jump instead (mean of the three good days after minus the three before). Grey dots are outlier days (left out of the line and the trend). Dotted vertical lines are M6+ earthquakes within 500 km. Scroll to zoom into days, double click to reset.
spec.title: Daily position of ${station:raw} · millimetres from its first day in the window

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per station and step of its path through the brush; the
-- transformations fold them back into one row per station, the path as an
-- array the table draws as a sparkline.
WITH area AS (
  SELECT list_transform(xs, lambda x: x - 360 * round(coalesce(list_avg(xs), 0) / 360)) AS xs, ys
  FROM (
    SELECT
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
      list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
    FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($area, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
  )
),
b AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t0 AS TIMESTAMP), min(time)) AS t0,
         coalesce(try_cast($t1 AS TIMESTAMP), max(time)) AS t1
  FROM $spark
),
ends AS (
  SELECT s.id, any_value(s.latitude) AS latitude, any_value(s.longitude) AS longitude,
         arg_min(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
         arg_max(s.east_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.east_mm IS NOT NULL) AS e1,
         arg_min(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
         arg_max(s.north_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.north_mm IS NOT NULL) AS n1,
         arg_min(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u0,
         arg_max(s.up_mm, s.time) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1 AND s.up_mm IS NOT NULL) AS u1,
         count(s.east_mm) FILTER (WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1) AS steps
  FROM $spark s, b
  GROUP BY s.id
),
d AS (
  SELECT id, latitude, longitude,
         e1 - e0 AS east_mm, n1 - n0 AS north_mm, u1 - u0 AS up_mm,
         sqrt((e1 - e0) ^ 2 + (n1 - n0) ^ 2) AS horizontal_mm,
         (degrees(atan2(e1 - e0, n1 - n0)) + 360) % 360 AS azimuth_deg,
         steps
  FROM ends
  -- a shift needs two steps: with one, start and end are the same day
  WHERE steps >= 2
),
nb AS (SELECT count(DISTINCT s.time) AS n FROM $spark s, b WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1),
t AS (
  SELECT d.id,
         round(d.horizontal_mm / 10, 2) AS horizontal_cm,
         CASE WHEN d.horizontal_mm IS NOT NULL THEN ['N', 'NE', 'E', 'SE', 'S', 'SW', 'W', 'NW'][(round(d.azimuth_deg / 45)::BIGINT % 8 + 1)::BIGINT] END AS toward,
         round(d.up_mm / 10, 2) AS up_cm,
         CASE WHEN date_diff('day', b.t0, b.t1) >= 365
              THEN round(d.horizontal_mm / (date_diff('day', b.t0, b.t1) / 365.25), 1) END AS mm_yr,
         round(100.0 * d.steps / nullif(nb.n, 0))::DOUBLE AS coverage_pct
  FROM d, b, nb, area
  WHERE (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
    CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > d.latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > d.latitude)
          AND d.longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (d.latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
         THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
),
p AS (
  SELECT s.id, s.time, sqrt((s.east_mm - e.e0) ^ 2 + (s.north_mm - e.n0) ^ 2) AS path
  FROM $spark s JOIN ends e ON e.id = s.id, b
  WHERE s.time BETWEEN b.t0 AND b.t1
)
SELECT t.*, p.time, p.path
FROM t LEFT JOIN p ON p.id = t.id
ORDER BY t.horizontal_cm DESC NULLS LAST, t.id, p.time

spec.description: Each station over the time brush: its horizontal shift in centimetres, the path that got it there (the horizontal distance from its first step in the brush, step by step), the compass direction, the vertical shift, the average rate in mm per year (only for a brush of a year or more), and the share of the brush's steps it has data for. Inside the drawn shape when there is one. A station name loads its series.
spec.title: Shift by station · over the time brush

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: the whole GNSS network for the dashboard's dates, plus each
-- station's catalog record.
--
-- The network endpoint answers only for the exact two days it is asked, and a
-- station without a position on one of them has no shift. So the window's ends
-- are tried a few days inward too (up to an eighth of the window, never more
-- than ten days, so a window around an earthquake never crosses it), and each
-- station keeps the outermost days it has. Asking past the newest published day
-- returns nothing at all, so the window is clamped to the catalog first.
WITH catalog AS (
  SELECT metadata.min_date::DATE AS first_day,
         metadata.max_date::DATE AS published,
         stations
  FROM read_json(
    'https://proj-sismos-source-files-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/summary_stations/parsed_data.json',
    maximum_object_size = 4000000
  )
),
win AS (
  SELECT greatest(CAST($__timeFrom() AS DATE), first_day) AS d0,
         least(CAST($__timeTo() AS DATE), published) AS d1,
         published
  FROM catalog
),
tries AS (
  SELECT k, d0 + (k * step)::INTEGER AS a, d1 - (k * step)::INTEGER AS b
  FROM (SELECT *, least(5, (d1 - d0) // 16)::INTEGER AS step FROM win), range(0, 3) t(k)
  WHERE k = 0 OR (step > 0 AND d0 + (k * step)::INTEGER < d1 - (k * step)::INTEGER)
),
layer AS (
  SELECT k, regexp_replace(r->>'body', '\bNaN\b', 'null')::JSON AS j
  FROM (
    SELECT k, http_get('https://d3l3n3l7bvxxh8.cloudfront.net/map_layer?start_date='
                       || strftime(a, '%Y-%m-%d') || '&end_date=' || strftime(b, '%Y-%m-%d')) AS r
    FROM tries
  )
  WHERE r->>'status' = '200'
),
raw AS (
  SELECT k, unnest(from_json(json_extract(j, '$.stations.stations'), '["JSON"]')) AS s FROM layer
),
ends AS (
  SELECT
    s->>'character_id' AS id, k,
    try_cast(s->>'y_location' AS DOUBLE) AS latitude,
    try_cast(s->>'x_location' AS DOUBLE) AS longitude,
    try_cast(json_extract_string(s, '$.limit_data.start_date.date') AS DATE) AS day0,
    try_cast(json_extract_string(s, '$.limit_data.start_date.d_e') AS DOUBLE) AS e0,
    try_cast(json_extract_string(s, '$.limit_data.start_date.d_n') AS DOUBLE) AS n0,
    try_cast(json_extract_string(s, '$.limit_data.start_date.d_u') AS DOUBLE) AS u0,
    try_cast(json_extract_string(s, '$.limit_data.end_date.date') AS DATE) AS day1,
    try_cast(json_extract_string(s, '$.limit_data.end_date.d_e') AS DOUBLE) AS e1,
    try_cast(json_extract_string(s, '$.limit_data.end_date.d_n') AS DOUBLE) AS n1,
    try_cast(json_extract_string(s, '$.limit_data.end_date.d_u') AS DOUBLE) AS u1
  FROM raw
),
best AS (
  SELECT id,
    any_value(latitude) AS latitude,
    any_value(longitude) AS longitude,
    arg_min(day0, k) FILTER (WHERE e0 IS NOT NULL AND n0 IS NOT NULL) AS start_day,
    arg_min(e0, k) FILTER (WHERE e0 IS NOT NULL AND n0 IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
    arg_min(n0, k) FILTER (WHERE e0 IS NOT NULL AND n0 IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
    arg_min(u0, k) FILTER (WHERE e0 IS NOT NULL AND n0 IS NOT NULL) AS u0,
    arg_min(day1, k) FILTER (WHERE e1 IS NOT NULL AND n1 IS NOT NULL) AS end_day,
    arg_min(e1, k) FILTER (WHERE e1 IS NOT NULL AND n1 IS NOT NULL) AS e1,
    arg_min(n1, k) FILTER (WHERE e1 IS NOT NULL AND n1 IS NOT NULL) AS n1,
    arg_min(u1, k) FILTER (WHERE e1 IS NOT NULL AND n1 IS NOT NULL) AS u1
  FROM ends
  GROUP BY id
),
-- How much of the window each station has data for, from the catalog's
-- availability spans: days with a position over days in the window.
spans AS (
  SELECT st.properties.id AS id,
         st.properties.min_date_registered::DATE AS since,
         st.properties.max_date_registered::DATE AS until,
         unnest(st.properties.availability) AS a
  FROM (SELECT unnest(stations) AS st FROM catalog)
),
cover AS (
  SELECT id, any_value(since) AS since, any_value(until) AS until,
    coalesce(sum(a.counts * greatest(0, (least(a.max_date::DATE, d1) - greatest(a.min_date::DATE, d0) + 1))
                 / (a.max_date::DATE - a.min_date::DATE + 1)), 0) / (d1 - d0 + 1) AS coverage
  FROM spans, win
  GROUP BY id, d0, d1
)
SELECT
  b.id, b.latitude, b.longitude,
  b.start_day::TIMESTAMP AS start_day,
  b.end_day::TIMESTAMP AS end_day,
  b.e1 - b.e0 AS east_m,
  b.n1 - b.n0 AS north_m,
  b.u1 - b.u0 AS up_m,
  sqrt((b.e1 - b.e0) ^ 2 + (b.n1 - b.n0) ^ 2) AS horizontal_m,
  -- Compass bearing of the shift, degrees clockwise from north.
  (degrees(atan2(b.e1 - b.e0, b.n1 - b.n0)) + 360) % 360 AS azimuth_deg,
  (b.end_day - b.start_day) / 365.25 AS years,
  least(c.coverage, 1) AS coverage,
  c.since::TIMESTAMP AS since,
  c.until::TIMESTAMP AS until,
  w.published::TIMESTAMP AS published
FROM best b
LEFT JOIN cover c USING (id)
CROSS JOIN win w
ORDER BY b.id

-- Server side: every M6+ earthquake USGS lists from Peru's south coast to Cape
-- Horn since the GNSS record starts (2013), about 120 events: loaded once,
-- filtered to the window in the browser.
SELECT
  to_timestamp(f.properties.time::BIGINT / 1000)::TIMESTAMP AS time,
  f.geometry.coordinates[2]::DOUBLE AS latitude,
  f.geometry.coordinates[1]::DOUBLE AS longitude,
  round(f.geometry.coordinates[3]::DOUBLE) AS depth_km,
  round(f.properties.mag::DOUBLE, 1) AS mag,
  f.properties.place::VARCHAR AS place,
  f.id::VARCHAR AS event_id
FROM (
  SELECT unnest(features) AS f
  FROM read_json(
    'https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query?format=geojson&starttime=2013-01-01&minmagnitude=6'
    || '&minlatitude=-60&maxlatitude=-15&minlongitude=-115&maxlongitude=-62&orderby=time-asc',
    maximum_object_size = 50000000
  )
)
ORDER BY time

-- Server side: the plate boundaries of Bird (2003), PB2002, the model GeoSismos
-- draws too, kept to the segments around South America.
LOAD spatial;
SELECT name, kind, geometry
FROM (
  SELECT f.properties.Name::VARCHAR AS name,
         -- PB2002 writes a subduction zone with a slash or a backslash between the
         -- two plates (NZ\SA: Nazca under South America) and anything else with a dash.
         CASE WHEN regexp_matches(f.properties.Name, '[/\\]') THEN 'subduction zone' ELSE 'other boundary' END AS kind,
         to_json(f.geometry)::VARCHAR AS geometry
  FROM (
    SELECT unnest(features) AS f
    FROM read_json('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fraxen/tectonicplates/master/GeoJSON/PB2002_boundaries.json',
                   maximum_object_size = 10000000)
  )
)
WHERE ST_Intersects(ST_GeomFromGeoJSON(geometry), ST_MakeEnvelope(-120, -65, -55, 5))

-- Server side: when each station has data, from the catalog's availability
-- spans: one row per unbroken run of days.
SELECT
  st.properties.id::VARCHAR AS id,
  st.properties.y_location::DOUBLE AS latitude,
  a.min_date::TIMESTAMP AS span_from,
  a.max_date::TIMESTAMP AS span_to,
  a.counts::DOUBLE AS days
FROM (
  SELECT unnest(stations) AS st
  FROM read_json('https://proj-sismos-source-files-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/summary_stations/parsed_data.json',
                 maximum_object_size = 4000000)
), unnest(st.properties.availability) AS u(a)
ORDER BY latitude DESC, span_from

-- Server side: every station's position through the window, from the file
-- datasets/geosismos/build.sh builds on each instance, in millimetres from its
-- first bucket in the window. Buckets are sized so a station has at most about
-- 120 of them (a day for windows up to four months, a week for two years...),
-- and each is the median of its good days.
--
-- An instance that has not run the build has no file, and read_parquet on a
-- missing URL fails the whole dataset, and with it every panel that reads it.
-- So the file is looked for first, and its absence reads as no rows: those
-- panels come up empty and the rest of the dashboard works.
SET VARIABLE positions = (
  SELECT CASE WHEN (http_head('http://feeds/datasets/geosismos/positions.parquet') ->> 'status') = '200'
              THEN 'SELECT id, latitude, longitude, day, east_mm, north_mm, up_mm '
                   || 'FROM read_parquet(''http://feeds/datasets/geosismos/positions.parquet'')'
              ELSE 'SELECT NULL::VARCHAR AS id, NULL::DOUBLE AS latitude, NULL::DOUBLE AS longitude, '
                   || 'NULL::TIMESTAMP AS day, NULL::DOUBLE AS east_mm, NULL::DOUBLE AS north_mm, '
                   || 'NULL::DOUBLE AS up_mm WHERE false'
         END
);
WITH step AS (
  SELECT CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMP) AS t0,
         CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMP) AS t1,
         greatest(1, ceil(date_diff('day', CAST($__timeFrom() AS TIMESTAMP), CAST($__timeTo() AS TIMESTAMP)) / 120))::INTEGER AS days
),
b AS (
  SELECT p.id, any_value(p.latitude) AS latitude, any_value(p.longitude) AS longitude,
         time_bucket(to_days(s.days), p.day, s.t0) AS time,
         median(p.east_mm) AS e, median(p.north_mm) AS n, median(p.up_mm) AS u
  FROM query(getvariable('positions')) p, step s
  WHERE p.day >= s.t0 AND p.day < s.t1
  GROUP BY p.id, time
),
base AS (
  SELECT id,
         arg_min(e, time) FILTER (WHERE e IS NOT NULL) AS e0,
         arg_min(n, time) FILTER (WHERE n IS NOT NULL) AS n0,
         arg_min(u, time) FILTER (WHERE u IS NOT NULL) AS u0
  FROM b
  GROUP BY id
)
SELECT b.id, b.latitude, b.longitude, b.time,
       round(b.e - base.e0, 1) AS east_mm,
       round(b.n - base.n0, 1) AS north_mm,
       round(b.u - base.u0, 1) AS up_mm,
       round(sqrt((b.e - base.e0) ^ 2 + (b.n - base.n0) ^ 2), 1) AS horizontal_mm
FROM b JOIN base USING (id)
ORDER BY b.latitude DESC, b.time
